title: Tear duct probing for babies
what: The doctor gently passes a thin probe through your baby's tear duct to open it. Tears can then drain into the nose again.
why: When your baby's eye keeps watering and getting sticky, and tear duct massage has not helped.
duration: the procedure itself usually takes a few minutes
tell_doctor: How long the eye has been watering and sticky
What drops and massage you have already tried
If your baby was ill recently or has a fever

prepare.title: Feeding
prepare.text: Ask the clinic when to feed your baby before the procedure.

prepare.title: Blanket
prepare.text: Bring a swaddling blanket. Babies are usually wrapped so they keep still.

prepare.title: Be ready
prepare.text: Your baby will cry. That is normal. The procedure is short.

bring: A bottle, or a way to feed your baby afterward
steps: The eye is numbed with drops
Your baby is wrapped, and an assistant helps hold the head
The doctor widens the tear duct opening and passes a thin probe
The duct is flushed with fluid
If the fluid reaches the nose, the duct is open
Your baby is handed back to you to soothe and feed
feel: Your baby cries, mostly from being held
A few drops of blood from the nose or eye can happen and pass
after: Use eye drops as your doctor prescribes
Massage the tear duct if your doctor says so
Come for a checkup when your doctor says
red_flags: Swelling and redness at the inner corner of the eye, or a fever
The eye has pus again a few days later: see a doctor

faq.q: Can it clear up without probing?
faq.a: It often clears on its own in the first months, especially with massage. The doctor decides when probing is needed.
The eye is numbed with drops. Babies mostly cry from being held.

faq.q: Will it need to be repeated?
faq.a: Usually once is enough. Sometimes it needs to be repeated.

reminders.text: Tear duct probing tomorrow. Bring a blanket and check when to feed your baby.
